intro: Sentence-final もの (casually もん) gives a reason as a self-justification: "because, you see", "well, it's that ...". The speaker is not just explaining but pleading for understanding, often after だって ("but"). The core image is a child folding their arms: "I didn't do my homework. I was tired, OK?"

skills.rule: End a plain-form sentence with もの / もん to give your reason as a plea for understanding: "because ..., you see", "but ..., OK?".
skills.explain:
もの at the end of a sentence turns a statement into an excuse or justification, usually for something you did, didn't do or won't do: 行きたくない。寒いもん (I don't want to go. It's cold). It is typical in answers to "why?" and is very often paired with だって at the start: だって、知らなかったんだもん (but I didn't know!).

Form: plain verbs and い-adjectives take it directly (眠いもん, 言ったもん); nouns and な-adjectives need だ (子供だもん, 好きだもん); んだもん is very common. もん is the everyday spoken form. もの sounds a little softer and more feminine, and ですもの is a dated, refined feminine polite form.

The tone is childish, sulky or affectionately cute, so it does not belong in formal speech or in excuses to a superior; there use ので or から in a normal sentence. Do not confuse it with ものだ ("that's how things are", "used to") or ものか ("as if!"), which are separate patterns.
patterns: [reason in plain form] もん / もの

examples.jp: 行[い]きたくない。寒[さむ]い{もん}。
examples.en: I don't want to go. It's cold.

examples.jp: ピーマンは食[た]べない。嫌[きら]いだ{もん}。
examples.en: I'm not eating the green peppers. I don't like them.

examples.jp: 仕方[しかた]ないよ。まだ子供[こども]だ{もの}。
examples.en: It can't be helped. He's still a child, after all.

examples.jp: だって、誰[だれ]も教[おし]えてくれなかったんだ{もん}。

contrast.note: から gives a reason neutrally and fits any register: 寒いから行かない. もん gives the same reason as a sulky or pleading excuse, only in casual speech: 行かない。寒いもん.
よ tells the listener something new: 寒いよ (it's cold, you know). もん justifies your own behaviour with it: 寒いもん (because it's cold, OK?).
ね seeks agreement on something shared: 寒いね. もん is not asking for agreement on the fact, but for sympathy with your excuse.

mistakes.bad: 仕方[しかた]ないよ。まだ子供[こども]{もん}。
mistakes.good: 仕方[しかた]ないよ。まだ子供[こども]だ{もん}。
mistakes.note: A noun or な-adjective needs だ before もん.

mistakes.bad: 部長[ぶちょう]、遅[おく]れてすみません。電車[でんしゃ]が止[と]まった{もん}。
mistakes.good: 部長[ぶちょう]、電車[でんしゃ]が止[と]まったので、遅[おく]れました。すみません。
mistakes.note: もん sounds childish. To a superior, give the reason with ので in a normal sentence.

skills.tip: Can you hear a sulky "...OK?" or "but ...!" at the end? Then もん.
